title: Sephiria Artifacts & Tablets — Inventory Grid Tips
description: Sephiria Artifact and Tablet guide: Side Bag rules, adjacency, and why tablet geometry beats raw rarity.
meta: Supports artifact / tablet searches; pairs with builds pages.
body:
Artifacts and Tablets are the mid-run puzzle. Tablets buff geometry (lines, crosses, columns). An Artifact outside an active pattern wastes space.

  • Side Bag storage disables effects—use it as a bench, not a secret second board.
  • Adjacency / edge / “no neighbors” constraints force full reshuffles after bosses.
  • Mystic Pot can convert leftover Artifacts (same rarity, or feed two to climb a rarity)—handy for awkward drops.

Bond artifacts: the ones that pay for two tags at once

A Bond artifact only switches on when the build already carries both of its tags. That makes them the cheapest way to convert a half-finished plan into a real one — and the fastest way to waste a slot if the second tag never arrives. The list below is the bond set recorded by the community artifact index; treat the pairings as the durable part and any per-level numbers as a snapshot.

Bond artifactNeeds both tagsWhat it is for
Scale of ConflictEmber + GlacierThe fire-and-ice bridge: one slot that keeps a split elemental board alive
Ruby BroochEmber + Storm CloudFire plus attack speed, for builds that want burn ticking faster
Rock ElephantGuardian + Wind SongDefence that still moves — pairs a defensive tag with the speed tag
Shield BagGuardian + AcademyTurns stacked defence into flat elemental damage
Tuning ForkAcademy + SturdySupport-side bond; only worth it once both tags already exist
Icebound TejasEmber + GlacierThe second fire-and-ice bond: two options, same tag pair
Thunderfrost ButterflyStorm Cloud + GlacierLightning plus cold, for freeze-and-zap boards
Droplet of PlitviceIce Armament + LakeWeapon-side ice bond, not an inventory-only effect
Tactical ManualCompanion + PrecisionCompanion damage routed through crit
Shimmering EyeShadow + PrecisionShadow crit bond for burst routes

Source: community artifact index (sephiriaguide.com), checked 9 November 2026. Tag pairings are the part worth relying on; the index is player-maintained, not official, and per-level values move between patches. Two bonds can share the same tag pair (Ember + Glacier has Scale of Conflict and Icebound Tejas), so the choice is about the secondary effect, not the tags.

Which bond for which plan

The same ten entries cut by the plan you are already running rather than by the item name. That is closer to how the decision is actually made at a shop screen, where the question is which plan the item completes rather than what the item is called.

The plan you are already runningBonds that fitWhat you get
Fire and ice in one boardScale of Conflict or Icebound TejasOne slot that holds a split elemental board together; the pair is identical, so choose on the secondary effect
Burn that ticks fasterRuby BroochFire plus attack speed
Defence that still movesRock ElephantA defensive tag married to the speed tag
Stacked defence turned into damageShield BagDefence converted into flat elemental damage
A support-side boardTuning ForkA support bond that only pays once both tags exist already
Freeze and shock togetherThunderfrost ButterflyLightning plus cold
A weapon-side ice routeDroplet of PlitviceIce Armament plus Lake, working from the weapon rather than the inventory alone
Companions doing the damageTactical ManualCompanion damage routed through crit
Shadow burstShimmering EyeShadow crit bond

A re-cut of the table above, not a second source: every row restates a pairing already listed, so nothing new is claimed. Where a plan is not on this list, the index has no bond for it, and the honest answer is that no bond is waiting to complete it.

One useful side effect of cutting the table this way is that it shows which tags are load-bearing. Ember and Glacier each appear in three of the ten bonds, which is why a fire or ice board has more ways to convert a spare slot than a Shadow or Companion board does:

TagBonds that use itCount
EmberScale of Conflict, Ruby Brooch, Icebound Tejas3
GlacierScale of Conflict, Icebound Tejas, Thunderfrost Butterfly3
Storm CloudRuby Brooch, Thunderfrost Butterfly2
GuardianRock Elephant, Shield Bag2
AcademyShield Bag, Tuning Fork2
PrecisionTactical Manual, Shimmering Eye2

Counted from the ten rows above; the remaining tags in the table — Wind Song, Sturdy, Lake, Ice Armament, Companion and Shadow — each appear once. This is arithmetic on the index, not a claim that the frequent tags are stronger. It only says that a board already running Ember or Glacier has more chances to turn a spare slot into a bond.

Bonds and the Wishing Fountain

The Wishing Fountain is the town picker where you load Artifacts before a run, and it is the one Artifact decision made outside the dungeon. It does not solve bonds. The builds page records a Steam discussion reporting that Bond Artifacts are not offered there, so the bond set has to be assembled from drops and shop stock inside the run.

That leaves the fountain with a narrower and more useful job: supply the single-tag pieces that make a bond reachable later. A pick taken in town that carries one of the two tags a bond needs is doing double duty, since the tag is what the bond checks. The caution is that the picker is chosen before the floor loads and nothing in the sources here describes changing it mid-run, so a pick taken for a bond that never materialises is capacity spent on nothing.

Capacity is the reason not to overload that plan. The reported default is 4, and the reported rarity costs run from 3 for a Common to 6 for a Legendary, so one expensive pick can use the whole bar. If the fountain is being used to pre-seed a bond, the pick has to be cheap enough to leave room for the rest of the set — see the fountain page for the capacity arithmetic and its caveats.

When a bond cannot be satisfied

The failure is the same every time: a slot is occupied by a bond whose second tag never arrived, so the plan is running one item short and does not know it. What to do depends on how far the run has gone:

MomentWhat to doWhy
The second tag is not in this run at allTreat the bond as an empty slot and stop buying toward the pairA half pair is worth nothing; the tag is what switches the effect on
Two bonds, same tag pairChoose on the secondary effect, not the tagsEmber + Glacier has two entries; the tags cannot separate them
The bond is already owned and the tag never cameTake it to the Mystic PotThe pot converts leftover Artifacts, which is the documented exit for awkward drops
The tag is reachable but only by crowding a live slotDecide which plan that slot servesA bond is one effect, and the slot it costs is the same slot another piece could use

The first two rows follow from how bonds work as described above; the last two from the Mystic Pot note on this page. None of it is a rule the client enforces for you.

Two records disagree slightly on what the pot does, and it is worth knowing before you plan around it. This page notes conversion at the same rarity, or two artifacts fed to climb a rarity. The secret-room record describes the pot as combining up to three deposited artifacts into one tablet. Those are not the same operation, so check the pot screen for the input count and the output before committing a bond you might still want.

How to use this page

  • Before a boss: count how many of your slots are bond artifacts whose second tag you do not have yet. Each one is dead weight.
  • When the shop offers a bond: check whether the missing tag is one you can still get from the current tablet layout. If not, skip it.
  • After a reshuffle: adjacency constraints change which slots are live, so re-check bonds before buying another artifact rather than after.

Which entries here are community-reported

All ten bond rows come from one player-maintained index, checked 9 November 2026. None of them is confirmed against an official artifact list, and the page prints no per-level values at all — that omission is deliberate, because those numbers move between patches and a stale number is worse than no number.

Read the columns at different strengths. The tag pair is the part the index supports directly, so it is the part to plan on. The one-line description of what each bond is for is a reading of that entry rather than a quoted effect, and the count table is arithmetic on those pairings. If your client disagrees with any of it, the client wins.

For the wider uncertainty, the editorial policy explains how this site sources pages and labels details that still need in-game verification. The same rule applies to the fountain capacity figures, which are community-reported and labelled as such.

What this page does not cover

  • Which weapon family to run. The six branches are on weapons; finished routes are on builds, and the summoner version is the Companion build.
  • How to load picks before a run. Order of operations and capacity caveats are on Wishing Fountain.
  • Why stored items go quiet. The Side Bag rule is on the beginner guide.
  • Where the leftover pieces come from. Room rewards and the pot are described on secret rooms.
  • Where the tags themselves come from. The permanent talent and unlock structure is on Destiny Inscription.

Quick FAQ

What makes an Artifact a bond?

It needs two tags at once. Until both are present the bond contributes nothing, which is why the pairings matter more than the item name.

Can I get a bond from the Wishing Fountain?

No. The builds page records a Steam discussion reporting that bonds are not offered there, so they have to be found or bought inside the run.

Does a bond work from the Side Bag?

No. Stored items do not contribute their effects, including Tablets, so a bond parked in the bag is not a bond.

Two bonds share Ember + Glacier. Which one?

Scale of Conflict or Icebound Tejas. The tags cannot choose for you, so pick on the secondary effect and on what the run already supports.

Can the Mystic Pot clean up a stranded bond?

It is the documented exit for leftover Artifacts, but the two records on this site describe different operations. Confirm the input count and output at the pot first.

Are the numbers on this page current?

There are no per-level numbers on this page on purpose. The index is player-maintained and values move between patches, so the pairings are the durable part.
